title: Mystery Blocks: On Your Own
subject: physical science
instructions: Answer on your own, even though you tested blocks with your group. Water's density is 1.0 g/cm³. Write your ID number, not your name.

questions.prompt: Find the Material: Work out each block's density, then name the material: pine 0.5, ice 0.92, aluminum 2.7, iron 7.9, lead 11.3 (g/cm³).
questions.notes: Density = mass ÷ volume. Look for 0.37 or 2 (volume ÷ mass) and a material that doesn't match the student's own density.

questions.prompt: Half a Block: A block with a mass of 80 g and a volume of 20 cm³ is cut in half. What is the density of each half?

options.why: Mass and volume both halve: the ratio stays.
Nothing got packed tighter by cutting.
Any piece of one material has the same density.

questions.skill: I can predict floating and sinking
questions.prompt: Heavy Log: A big log weighs more than a small rock, yet the log floats and the rock sinks. Why?

options.why: A heavy iron bar sinks; weight alone doesn't decide.

options.text: The log is bigger, so it floats.
options.why: A big rock still sinks; compare mass per volume.

options.text: The log is less dense than water, and the rock is denser.
Rocks always sink, whatever their density.
options.why: Pumice is a rock that floats: it's less dense.

questions.skill: I can predict floating and sinking
questions.prompt: Ice: Ice is water that froze. Use density to explain why ice floats on liquid water.
questions.key: Ice's density (about 0.92 g/cm³) is less than liquid water's (1.0 g/cm³), because water expands when it freezes (same mass, more volume); anything less dense than water floats. Full credit needs the comparison of densities; adding why it's less dense is a strength, not required. 'Ice is lighter' alone is partial.
